Project: /home/alex/Projects/FALA — FALA, a European Portuguese CLI tutor (Python 3.10+).
Key files: config.py (module-level path constants: DATA_DIR, SUMMARY_PATH, VOCABULARY_PATH, SESSIONS_DIR, RECORDS_DIR),
progress.py (imports those constants; functions load_summary/save_summary/load_vocabulary/save_vocabulary/get_review_words/update_vocab_after_review/add_vocabulary/save_learning_record/get_vocab_for_prompt/vocabulary_report),
conversation.py (ConversationEngine — calls progress functions, owns session lifecycle),
web.py (FastAPI prototype: single GLOBAL engine + module-level _session_started/_session_ended booleans — this is what we are replacing),
fala.py (CLI entrypoint — must keep working unchanged from a user's perspective).
Tests: run with: cd /home/alex/Projects/FALA && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q   (77 currently green)
Lint/type: cd /home/alex/Projects/FALA && scripts/lint.sh   (ruff + ruff format + mypy — must stay clean)
Python 3.10 syntax. Do NOT modify audio.py or prompts/. Do NOT weaken existing tests.


Design decisions (already made — implement these, don't re-litigate):
1. Per-user data layout: data/users/<user_id>/{summary.md, vocabulary.md, sessions/, records/} for non-default users.
2. The special user id "default" maps to the EXISTING flat data/ paths (no file migration, zero risk to current CLI behavior). This is how the existing single-user data "becomes the default user".
3. config.py gains a paths resolver, e.g. paths_for_user(user_id: str) -> dict or small dataclass with summary/vocabulary/sessions/records/data-dir entries, creating dirs as needed. Existing module-level constants stay for backward compat.
4. progress.py functions gain an optional paths parameter (default = current behavior). Thread paths through rather than reading config globals at call time.
5. ConversationEngine.__init__ gains user_id: str = "default" (or a paths object) and passes resolved paths to every progress call. CLI (fala.py) keeps using the default user.
6. web.py: replace global engine + booleans with a session store: dict[str, SessionState] keyed by a "fala_session" cookie (uuid4, httponly, set on first request if absent). SessionState holds user_id, engine (ConversationEngine | None), session_started/ended flags, last_active. For now user_id == the session id (invite-code auth in a later phase will bind real user ids). /start creates an engine for that user; /quit and "quit"/"exit"/"sair" in /message end it and clear the engine so a new /start works. Concurrent users must never share an engine.
7. No idle-session reaper needed yet — leave a TODO comment.

Task: implement items 1-5 (config paths resolver, progress.py paths threading, ConversationEngine user_id). Keep CLI behavior byte-identical for the default user. Add focused tests: paths resolver (default vs named user), per-user vocab isolation through ConversationEngine (mock LLM calls as existing tests do — check tests/conftest.py for the established pattern). Run the full test suite and scripts/lint.sh; iterate until 100% green. Return a concise summary: files changed, tests added, final pytest/lint status.
